ticket: python lint.py (what make lint runs) checks files that the docs build itself skips. Repro: add a third-party folder under docs/, say vendor/ holding the upstream LICENSE.txt, and add "vendor" to exclude_patterns in docs/conf.py. make html leaves it out, as expected. Actual: make lint still reads vendor/LICENSE.txt and reports sphinx-lint errors in it, so the docs lint job fails on a file that is not part of the documentation. Expected: make lint never reports on a file the docs build excludes; it still checks every file the docs build includes, with the same enabled and disabled checks, the 79-character line limit, and any extra arguments passed to lint.py.
guess:
Fix `lint.py` to filter by `docs/conf.py:exclude_patterns`:

```py
import importlib.util, fnmatch, sys
from pathlib import Path
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("conf","docs/conf.py")
conf=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec);spec.loader.exec_module(conf)
excl=getattr(conf,"exclude_patterns",[])
files=[str(p) for p in Path("docs").rglob("*") if p.is_file() and not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(str(p),pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(p.name,pat) for pat in excl)]
```

Then run `sphinx-lint --max-line-length 79` with same `enable/disable` checks on `files + sys.argv[1:]` instead of unfiltered `docs/`.

In `lint.py` filter by `docs/conf.py:exclude_patterns` and forward `argv`:

```diff

+import sys,fnmatch; sys.path.insert(0,"docs")
+from conf import exclude_patterns
+def excluded(p): return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(str(p),pat) for pat in exclude_patterns)
+files=[p for p in Path("docs").rglob("*") if not excluded(p)]
 
-run(["sphinx-lint","--enable","all","--disable","...","--max-line-length","79"]+files)

```
